title: Release Authorization Policy for Medical Records Requests
content:
## Policy

1. Where the Medical Records Requests type requires a signed release authorization, no work starts until the patient, or a documented personal representative, signs a release authorization naming the recipient. Signing is the patient's own act; only the patient or the legal representative can give it.
2. Where the type requires representative documentation, a representative supplies guardianship, power-of-attorney or estate documentation.
3. The authorization is returned signed no later than the type's return window counted from the date it was requested. The window is counted in calendar days starting the day after the request date, and a signature on the last day still qualifies.
4. An authorization not returned in time lapses, and the request is cancelled with the reason "authorization not returned".
5. A signed authorization stays valid until the expiration it states or, if it states none, the type's validity period in calendar months after signing.
6. Where the type requires a new authorization for a change of recipient, a different recipient needs a new authorization and a new request.
7. A patient's own copy requests, and provider-to-provider transfers for treatment, need no authorization.

While a requested authorization is outstanding the request stands in status authorization pending; when the patient signs, the request moves to in process.

## The return window, broken down

| Element | Content |
|---|---|
| Clock starts from | The date the authorization was requested, as shown on the request record |
| Counting | Calendar days, day 1 being the day after the request date |
| Comparison | The signature is dated no later than the last day of the window |
| Last day itself | Qualifies (inclusive) |
| Not met | The authorization lapses; the request is cancelled with the reason "authorization not returned" |

## Worked dates (hypothetical, on a type with a 30-day return window and a 12-month validity period)

- Authorization requested on 10 April. Day 1 is 11 April, so day 30, the last day of the window, is 10 May.
- Signed on 10 May: on the last day, so it qualifies.
- Not signed by the end of 10 May: the authorization lapses, and the request is cancelled with the reason "authorization not returned"; a signature on 11 May is out of time.
- Signed on 10 May and stating no expiration: valid until 10 May of the following year. If it states an expiration of its own, it is valid until that stated expiration.

## Basis questions

**Can a support agent or a relative who holds no representative documentation sign for the patient?** No. Signing is the patient's own act, or that of a documented personal representative.

**Does a patient asking for a copy of their own records need to sign a release authorization?** No. A patient's own copy requests need no authorization.
